page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-192 is an enterprise instance within the network-optimized server family, configured for high-capacity multithreaded execution. The system runs on 64-bit x86_64 architecture and supplies 192 dedicated virtual processor cores paired with 720 GB of system memory. This configuration provides an allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The machine includes zero integrated local storage drives, requiring persistent disk attachments over the network for data storage, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or discrete GPU hardware.

In terms of resource architecture and cost efficiency, the c4n-standard-192 consolidates extensive CPU execution capacity into a single high-density virtual node. By omitting costly hardware components such as dedicated machine learning accelerators and local NVMe solid-state disks, organizations avoid expenditure on unused silicon when their primary constraints are processing concurrency and network connectivity. The 3.75 GB per core balance supports compute throughput while maintaining sufficient memory buffers for large-scale multithreaded runtime environments.

Workload suitability centers on network-intensive, heavily multithreaded enterprise environments that do not require physical hardware acceleration or on-board ephemeral storage. Typical deployments include distributed backend application services, large microservice aggregation layers, real-time message brokering, batch extract-transform-load processing pipelines, and high-throughput network appliance functions.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-192 is a network-optimized compute instance designed for intensive parallel workloads and high-throughput communication. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine supplies 192 dedicated vCPUs and 720 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage, relying on external network storage volumes for persistence, and it excludes discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Without hardware graphics accelerators or attached local NVMe drives, resource utilization is strictly focused on raw CPU parallelism and memory capacity. From an infrastructure cost-efficiency standpoint, the dense 192-core profile consolidates massive multithreaded capacity onto a single node, lowering management overhead for horizontally scaled enterprise architectures. The c4n-standard-192 server is structured for distributed services, large-scale web serving tiers, data transformations, network traffic routing, backend application engines, and scale-out parallel computation.
